candidates.explanation: Capability behavior is coherently colocated, with justified framework and observability surfaces. The application operation and provider port are framework/provider neutral. The Route Handler correctly handles abort propagation, rolling idle timeout, pre/post-commit failures, safe redaction, and no partial-stream retry. HTTP, SSE, and jobs retain native lifecycle contracts while sharing semantics.

The lifecycle and boundary design is strong: dedicated SSE Route Handler, cancellation, resettable idle timeout, commit-aware failure handling, native job decisions, safe provider isolation, and no stream replay. However, assistant behavior is fragmented across top-level domain, ports, adapters, use-cases, boundary, infrastructure, and UI roots rather than colocated under one capability root.

The proposal correctly defines a framework-neutral use case and provider port, uses a dedicated SSE Route Handler, propagates cancellation, implements a rolling idle timeout, changes failure representation after commit, reports unexpected failures once, and preserves job-native retry/dead-letter semantics. Its main deficiency is scattering the capability across domain, use-cases, adapters, infrastructure, UI, and app roots.

The capability is centered under src/modules/assistant with only the framework route outside it. It clearly separates the framework-neutral generation operation from a capability-shaped provider port, keeps provider details private, and gives HTTP streaming and jobs native interpreters. Cancellation, rolling idle timeout, safe pre/post-commit failure handling, exactly-once reporting, and retry discipline are all coherent.
